gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 identifies a missing two-fold-uniformity hypothesis when applying a variance theorem to a general coarse-scrambling corollary. It does not identify the distinct defect in the block-affine construction: Delta_j is left with no distribution, permitting Delta_j=0 and thereby destroying uniformity of the construction itself.

Both entries identify the inconsistent normalization of the weighted double-sum gain: the definition contains an extra sample-size factor, so the stated gain formulas and downstream variance identities do not agree. ISSUE-003 specifically recognizes the erroneous factor in the G-tilde definition and supplies the corresponding correction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The gain quantities are normalized inconsistently by powers of n. In particular, the leading 1/n in the G-tilde definition makes the definition disagree with the variance theorem and exact gain identities; removing or consistently relocating that factor restores the intended formulas.

component_coverage.gold_component: The weighted double-sum gain is defined with an incorrect sample-size normalization, producing incompatibility between its definition, the variance theorem, and downstream gain identities.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the normalization factors in C and G-tilde as inconsistent with the displayed formulas and later computations, and explicitly repairs the G-tilde factor. This directly diagnoses the gold normalization defect and its effect on subsequent identities.
